title: Rail launcher
goal_text: A latched plunger on a rail is pressed back against a coil spring with a ball resting against its face. When the drive phase starts the latch opens and the spring, helped by the linear actuator, throws the plunger forward; past the spring's rest point the plunger slows down, the ball runs on alone along the rail, leaves the open end and flies to the floor. Choose the pull-back distance and the actuator command so that the ball first touches the floor at the target distance measured along +y from the centre of the table.
manual:
Device 'rail_launcher' (5 parts). Coordinates in metres, z up, ground at z=0. Joint coordinates are 0 in the pose described here.
Parts:
- table: box 0.120 x 0.400 x 0.500 m, concrete, mass 57.600 kg; centre (0.000, 0.000, 0.250), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.060, -0.200, 0.000)..(0.060, 0.200, 0.500); rests on the ground, fixed in place
- track: box 0.120 x 0.400 x 0.020 m, wood, mass 0.624 kg; centre (0.000, 0.000, 0.510), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.060, -0.200, 0.500)..(0.060, 0.200, 0.520); rigidly fixed to 'table'
- stand: box 0.080 x 0.060 x 0.580 m, aluminium, mass 7.517 kg; centre (0.160, 0.105, 0.290), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (0.120, 0.075, 0.000)..(0.200, 0.135, 0.580); rests on the ground, fixed in place
- plunger: box 0.150 x 0.060 x 0.016 m, wood, mass 0.094 kg; centre (0.045, 0.105, 0.545), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.030, 0.075, 0.537)..(0.120, 0.135, 0.553); slide joint to 'stand' at (0.120, 0.105, 0.545), axis (0.000, 1.000, 0.000), rail model, end stops [-0.340, 0.000] m, coil_stiff spring relaxed at -0.100
- ball: sphere radius 0.025 m, steel, sealed, mass unknown (between 0.3 and 0.9 kg); centre (0.000, 0.160, 0.545), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.025, 0.135, 0.520)..(0.025, 0.185, 0.570); loose (free body), carried by 'plunger' when it is set up
Actuators (command in [-1, 1]):
- drive: linear_actuator driving 'plunger'
Latches (hold the joint at its starting value until released):
- hold: locks 'plunger'
Sensors (Gaussian noise, standard deviation):
- plunger_x: joint_angle of 'plunger', noise 0.002
- plunger_v: joint_velocity of 'plunger', noise 0.01
- ball_v: velocity of 'ball', noise 0.01
- ball_p: position of 'ball', noise 0.002
Physics: rigid bodies with soft contacts, gravity 9.81 m/s^2 along -z. Contact friction between two surfaces is the larger of their two coefficients. Unknowns of scope 'world' are properties of a material or of a catalog part model (bearing, rail, spring, motor type): they are identical in every device and every instance in this world. Unknowns of scope 'device' belong to this device and are drawn anew for every instance.
Before each run: joint of 'plunger' is set to knob 'pullback'
Action program (then all commands 0 until the end): phase 0: lasts 0.5 s; commands [drive = knob 'drive']; release hold at start | phase 1: lasts 2 s; commands [none]

knobs.name: pullback
knobs.description: plunger position on its rail before release; more negative pulls the plunger (and the ball with it) further back and compresses the spring more

knobs.name: drive
knobs.description: command held on the linear actuator during the drive phase; it pushes the plunger forward alongside the spring

unknowns.name: ball_mass
unknowns.description: sealed mass of the launched ball

outcome.description: the y coordinate(s) of 'ball' at the moment it first touches the ground

rules:
Protocol (enforced by the lab tool):
1. Pretest: you get 3 goals one at a time and must choose knob values for each
   before running any experiment on this device. Results are revealed only at the end.
2. Lab: up to 70 experiments. Every experiment requires your prediction of the
   outcome before you see the result. Every 10th experiment is chosen by the referee:
   you are told the knob values, you predict, then you see the result.
3. Theory: submit predict.py defining predict(knobs: dict, visible: dict) -> list[float],
   your model of the outcome. `visible` holds the modifiable dimensions listed below; the
   referee may evaluate your model with different values for them, without letting you
   experiment. Also submit your estimates of the unknown quantities with 90% intervals.
4. Exam: 8 goals one at a time, one attempt each, no experiments. Results are
   revealed only at the end.
5. Field report: optional tickets about the interface (bugs, ambiguity, suspected
   unsolvability). Tickets go to the device builder; they cannot contain answers.
Outcome is a failure if the run status is not "ok" (e.g. the part never landed, or was
still moving at the end of the run).
